# Contributors {#sec-contributions}

### How to contribute {.unnumbered}

We welcome suggestions for new contributions, from small fixes or
updates to entire chapters. Instructions for contributors can be found
in the OMA
[README](https://github.com/microbiome/OMA/blob/devel/README.md#development-and-contributions).

### Key developers and coordinators {.unnumbered}

The book and its associated package ecosystem are a highly collaborative
effort involving dozens of developers and contributors.

Contributions to this book are coordinated by [Leo
Lahti](http://www.iki.fi/Leo.Lahti) and Tuomas Borman at the [Department
of Computing, University of Turku,
Finland](https://datascience.utu.fi/). Both have served on the
[Bioconductor Community Advisory
Board](https://bioconductor.org/about/community-advisory-board/) and run
regular training workshops in microbiome data science.

### Background of the book {.unnumbered}

The framework for microbiome data science presented in this book is
based on specialized data containers for hierarchical and multi-omic
data sets. The `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("TreeSummarizedExperiment")` data
container for single-omic data was created by
@R_TreeSummarizedExperiment, and the
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("MultiAssayExperiment")` container for multi-omic
data by @Ramos2017. The idea of using these containers as a basis for
microbiome data science was initiated by Domenick Braccia, Héctor
Corrada Bravo, Felix Ernst, and others, and brought together with other
microbiome data science developers [@Shetty2019; @Ernst2020]. Setting up
the base ecosystem of packages and tutorials was subsequently led by
Tuomas Borman, Felix Ernst, and Leo Lahti. Lahti had earlier developed
the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("phyloseq")`-based
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("microbiome")` R package before switching to the
(Tree)SE/MAE-based framework and the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`
family of Bioconductor packages introduced in this book. Many
contributors then advanced the ecosystem further. Ample data resources
were made available through the
[curatedMetagenomicData](https://waldronlab.io/curatedMetagenomicData/)
project by Edoardo Pasolli, Lucas Schiffer, Levi Waldron, and others
[@Pasolli2017], and through data retrieval packages such as
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("HoloFoodR")` and
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("MGnifyR")`. The
[tidyomics](https://github.com/tidyomics) project [@Hutchison2024] made
it easier to build omic data analysis workflows.

The online book was initially set up by Leo Lahti, Felix Ernst, and
Tuomas Borman. Additional chapters were subsequently contributed by
Christian L. Müller and Stefanie Peschel (network analysis); Himel
Mallick, Nalin Arora and Yihan Liu (multi-omics and mediation); Matti
Ruuskanen (machine learning); and Thomaz F. S. Bastiaanssen and Benjamin
Valderrama (utilization of pathway and other side information); and Aura
Raulo, Giulio Benedetti, Geraldson Muluh (contributions across various
chapters). Jacques Serizay converted the *OMA* book to the
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("BiocBook")` format, which allows it to be built
and distributed by Bioconductor. The work of many contributors is
acknowledged in the related publications and can be tracked at
the respective GitHub repositories. We welcome suggestions for updates
to this historical account, and thank everyone who has contributed to
this growing toolkit of microbiome data science methods (see
[@sec-ecosystem]).

The work drew initial inspiration from many sources, most notably from
the work on `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("phyloseq")` by Paul McMurdie and
Susan Holmes [@McMurdie2013], who pioneered rigorous and reproducible
microbiome data science ecosystems in R/Bioconductor. The
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("phyloseq")` framework continues to provide a vast
array of complementary packages and methods for microbiome studies. The
*Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis with Bioconductor*
([*OSCA*](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA/)) book by Robert
Amezquita, Aaron Lun, Stephanie Hicks, and Raphael Gottardo
[@Amezquita2020natmeth] presents related work on the
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SummarizedExperiment")` data container and its
derivatives in single-cell sequencing studies, which inspired this work.
The open-source books *Modern Statistics for Modern Biology* by Susan
Holmes and Wolfgang Huber [@Holmes2019], *R for Data Science* by Garrett
Grolemund and Hadley Wickham [@Grolemund2017], and *Statistical
Rethinking* by Richard McElreath, with the associated online resources
by Solomon Kurz [@McElreath2020], are key references that have advanced
reproducible data science training and dissemination.

(CompLifeSci) Research Program of [Biocity
